conviction.explanation: 28% revenue growth and positive H1 FCF preserve recovery upside, but margin compression survives charge addbacks and H1 FCF fell 30.3%. Substantial future capex and lease demands make 21.17x forward earnings insufficient by itself to favor adding.

executive_summary:
Meta’s advertising franchise is growing: impressions rose 14%, ad pricing 12% and revenue 28%; H1 CFO was$64.088bn. H1 FCF remained positive at$13.170bn, supporting an internally generated recovery resource.

Q2 FCF was only$0.784bn and H1 FCF declined 30.3%. Illustrative legal/severance addbacks still leave margin below the prior 43%, while$130–145bn capex guidance raises the productivity hurdle. Neutral reflects measured conversion pressure and slowing momentum; legal costs are not assumed to vanish.
bull_case: Monetization growth and productive infrastructure could restore margins and cash available to owners at a more moderate forward multiple.
bear_case: Investment, leases and continuing legal costs could absorb advertising gains and depress owner cash despite strong sales.
key_uncertainties: Incremental capex productivity and cash recovery.
Recurring legal spending and comparable margins.
Lease demands beyond the partial liquid-assets/debt comparison.
catalysts_upcoming: Next results: cash conversion recovering alongside impression/pricing growth would strengthen the recovery thesis.
Capital-spending and expense disclosures showing costs stabilize relative to monetization would improve owner economics.
